newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD says set to apply for cell phone frequencies.
newsitem.headline: KDD says set to apply for cell phone frequencies.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd said on Monday it plans to apply for government approval on use of radio frequencies in 1999 to enter the next-generation cellular phone business.

Japan's top international call carrier said earlier that it expects next-generation cell phones, which are expected to be able to transfer pictures, to be available in the marketplace by the beginning of 2001.
KDD also said it has not decided on the format for the CDMA cellular phone technology to be used in its next-generation cell phones.

Industry officials said there was a tug-of-war in the Japanese phone industry between a cell phone format being developed by Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's NTT DoCoMo and another CDMA format promoted by Motorola Inc of the United States.
